title: Reserved capacity economics - sensitivity sheet
description: Working spreadsheet used to model economics of Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) commits. Contains per-commit size bands, utilization sensitivity, blended unit cost calculations, recommended pricing tiers, early-termination policy impact, and operational playbook notes for sales/finance alignment.
assumptions: Base GPU list price (on-demand equivalent) = $3.50/hour per A100-80GB equiv
Committed discount applies to gross GPU-hour cost before platform fee
Platform fee = 18% of raw GPU cost (applies to hosted and dedicated management components)
Average request profile: 4k tokens per generation, 1.2 calls/sec per GPU equivalent at target latency
Burst buffer (uncommitted spare capacity) allowed = 15% of provisioned GPUs, charged at on-demand marginal rate
Customer types modeled: AI-startup (high-growth), Mid-market SaaS (predictable), Enterprise (SLA + long-term)

conclusion: Preliminary recommendation: introduce three commit bands (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) with blended-per-GPU-hr pricing that scales down with commit size. Require minimum 3mo for Starter, 12mo for Enterprise. Offer a short free burst allowance and tiered early-termination penalties. Key next step: run these bands against 20 anonymized customer usage profiles (solutions-eng) to validate break-even util thresholds before finalizing pricing.
notes_for_finance: Finance should validate platform fee assumptions and run contract-level cashflow: deferred revenue for prepayments, expected churn-adjusted utilization. Model tax implications on early-termination credits and any promotional credits.
